applied.summary: INV-1 named redactSecrets (cli-anything/src/redact.ts:62) as the credential control, but it only masks parent-env values under secret-ish key names — a key read via pi's !-prefix indirection out of ~/.pi/agent/auth.json is never in the env and passes through unredacted; no src/ -> cli-anything/src/ import exists anywhere in the repo (module_roots keeps KEEP assets in cli-anything/*). Rewrote INV-1 around non-interpolation, stated the redaction limitation explicitly, and made the DoD security item a seeded-sentinel-key test.

Slug resolution was undefined: the schema has both a `provider` field and a `model` documented as `provider/id`, and real model ids contain `/` (this host's registered model is id deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 under provider openrouter, R4 4.2). AC1 is make-or-break on 'resolve each slug' with no resolution rule. Added the rule (provider authoritative; first-`/` split only when provider absent; contradicting prefix is a validation error), retitled AC1 to `(provider, model)` pairs, added a DoD slug-resolution test.

Technical Notes stated a behavior — 'Validation warns when a role declares extensions and a non-null tools list' (the --tools silently filters extension tools landmine, R4 1.5 / sssf.config.yaml:9-11) — with no AC and no DoD coverage. Folded the warning assertion into the unit-test DoD item.

Fail-fast collect-all list named 'missing prompt file', but prompt_engineering is not in this story's schema (deliberate subset of SSSF's AgentConfig). Replaced with 'duplicate role name', which is in-schema.

Exit-code precedence undefined when a collect-all run yields both a rejected slug (exit 1) and an unevaluable gate (exit 2). Specified that 2 dominates 1 — an unevaluated gate is not a complete verdict — with rejections still listed in the report.

Schema claimed 'field set and semantics follow R4 1.5' while dropping four SSSF fields (coding_agent, color, purpose, prompt_engineering) and adding an explicit `provider`. Restated as a deliberate subset plus `provider` so the deviation is intentional, not an omission.

Removed the speculative pluggable listModels(provider) seam sentence — one provider is in scope today and the abstraction was unrequested; also removed the unverifiable '23 tests' count on cli-args.ts (83 lines verified, test count did not match).

DoD required the raw NDJSON capture 'written through writeArtifactAtomic at mode 0600' — unsatisfiable as written: the helper JSON.stringify's its payload, force-appends .json, enforces /^[\w.-]+$/ on the name and sets no mode (verified cli-anything/src/team-events.ts:138-161), and team-events.ts is not in Files to Modify. Split the two write paths: raw capture via writeFileSync(..., {mode: 0o600}) into QDS_TEAM_RAW_WORKER_DIR; the JSON verdict artifact keeps writeArtifactAtomic unchanged, with team-events.ts explicitly untouched.

The make-or-break AC1's central quantity, 'the measured ratio', was never defined (no numerator/denominator), and a raw first-turn-input ratio is confounded by task-prompt size: the 5-6x hypothesis concerns the 37,279-token overhead term, so a large prompt inflates both arms' totals and can record `refuted` while the lever worked exactly as claimed. Defined ratio = control mean first-turn input tokens / lean mean (per worker then aggregated) and required per-worker absolute `deltaTokens` in the artifact; wired deltaTokens into AC1, the E2E slice and the DoD e2e item.

AC2 did not pin argv position for --no-extensions/--no-skills or the -e pairs, yet AC3 and the DoD demand a byte-exact 9-element argv diff. Pinned the order: lean flags then one -e <path> pair per allowlist entry, all inserted before -p, which stays last and still carries ${w.prompt}\n\n${schemaInstruction} (verified team-lead-driver.ts:129-141).

INV-1 said capture files are created 'under artifacts/' while AC5 gates capture on the operator-chosen QDS_TEAM_RAW_WORKER_DIR — a direct contradiction about where bytes land. Resolved in the INV-1 rewrite: files go into that directory.

The story implied --no-extensions and --no-skills are symmetric. R4 4.1 verbatim: --no-skills disables discovery *and loading*, so no explicit --skill survives lean, unlike -e paths under --no-extensions. Named the asymmetry and scoped a skills allowlist out, so a future roster cannot assume symmetry.

Traced the lead's coms concern to code: on the proven local path 'coms' is subprocess-RPC the driver synthesizes (team-lead-driver.ts:14-15, :42), not a pi extension, and workers get no -e at all — so --no-extensions cannot regress coms today. Stated this so an implementer does not hunt for a coms extension to preserve; AC2's -e survival assertion remains as protection for the future coms-net case.
Corrected the presence-only key-logging citation from runner.ts:547-550 to :548-551 (verified), in both the Infra Prerequisites table and INV-4.
Noted in Guards/limits that runner.ts:546 overwrites PI_COMS_TIMEOUT_MS from the manifest, so the bench harness cannot set the per-run timeout via the parent env — it must come from the manifest.

surviving.summary: AC2's shallow-merge citation MOD/agents.py:33-41 points into the out-of-repo SSSF reference tree (REFERENCE ONLY per R5 6 fact 20), so it cannot be verified from this repo; it is correctly transcribed from R4 1.5, which quotes the source verbatim.

DoD enumerates thinking levels 'from pi 0.55.0' while Infra Prerequisites records the local tree running pi libs 0.55.4 (vendor dir peer-pins 0.55.0). The --help evidence in R4 4.3 is from 0.55.0; the residual risk is a 0.55.4 level set that differs, which the preflight version assertion would not catch.

AC3 renders today's argv as `-p <prompt>` without spelling out the \n\n${schemaInstruction} suffix; AC2 and the 9-element DoD boundary test both pin it exactly, so the ambiguity cannot survive into the implementation.
